2.definition: A legacy volumetric mode of the previous two-stage module version that used triplets of consecutive slices (z-1, z, z+1) to predict the center slice; imported 2.5D models remain usable for inference

G.definition: A smoothing filter using weights that follow a bell curve (Gaussian) distribution, giving more weight to nearby pixels
Human-created labels that represent the correct answer, used to train and evaluate machine learning models
GL Transmission Format (binary .glb), a modern 3D mesh format exportable through file-browser conversion.

Q.definition: Measuring segmented objects: voxel counts, physical volume, connected components, component sizes and surface area.

S.definition: A training approach where the model learns from the data itself without requiring manually labeled ground truth
Temporary file storage that exists only during your login session — files are cleared when the session ends
The standard deviation of the Gaussian distribution - controls how quickly weights decrease with distance
A single 2D image within a 3D image stack, typically representing one focal plane or time point
A one-pixel-wide, 180-degree symmetric mask tracing the significant lines of the noise autocorrelation, used by the StructN2V branch of autoStructN2V
Stereolithography format - a common file format for 3D printing that stores triangle mesh geometry
Noise with spatial patterns or correlations, such as scan lines or periodic artifacts, as opposed to random pixel-independent noise
A 3D representation composed of vertices (points) and faces (triangles) that approximate the surface of an object
The saved per-stack placements from a stitch; reusable on sibling volumes of the same geometry without re-aligning.
Joins several stacks into one volume through z-concatenation, z-overlap or xy mosaics using a saved placement recipe.
Edits and measures a segmentation on a working copy: painting, automated cleanup and quantification, saving the result as a new file.

D.definition: The process of removing unwanted noise from images while preserving important features and details
A directionality statistic computed from the noise autocorrelation; values at or above 0.012 route autoStructN2V training to the StructN2V branch

B.definition: An action performed on multiple selected files at once, such as batch download or batch delete
A network architecture that cannot see the center pixel when predicting it, preventing the trivial solution of copying noisy values
A painting tool that applies the current class label to pixels as you draw

A.definition: A labeled mask where each pixel is assigned to a class (background or object categories)
A self-supervised extension of N2V that measures the noise autocorrelation on the raw images and routes automatically between structured masking (StructN2V) and plain N2V

W.definition: The collection of all files in your current session, organized into categories for different processing stages
A compressed archive containing your entire workspace, used for backup and restore between sessions
A server-side editable copy of a segmentation used by the cleanup module; the original file is never modified.

I.definition: A series of 2D images stored together, representing a 3D volume or time series

M.definition: An algorithm that extracts a polygonal mesh from a 3D scalar field (like a labeled image stack) by finding surface boundaries
An image where pixel values represent class labels rather than visual intensity
The sum of squared correlations over the mask's off-center positions; the fraction of the center pixel's noise variance the mask covers
The automatic discovery of a structural noise mask (spine) from the noise autocorrelation measured on background regions of the raw stack
A 3D surface representation composed of vertices (points) and faces (triangles)
A volume file format common in electron microscopy; importable as raw or annotation stacks and produced by format conversion.
Stacks that tile the same depth range side by side in x/y, joined into one wider volume by the stitching module.

C.definition: A category of pixels in a segmentation task, such as 'cell', 'background', or 'nucleus'
Limiting the visible region of a 3D object to reveal internal structure

P.definition: Moving the viewing area across a zoomed image by clicking and dragging
A small rectangular region of pixels used for comparison in NLM denoising
Polygon File Format, a mesh geometry format exportable through file-browser conversion.
Prepares a grayscale stack for the pipeline: crop, z-trim, flip/rotate, downscale, intensity adjustment and bit-depth conversion.

N.definition: The correlation of the noise with itself at different pixel offsets, measured on detrended background tiles; the basis for routing and mask discovery in autoStructN2V
A self-supervised denoising method that trains by predicting masked pixels from their surroundings, requiring no clean reference images
A denoising algorithm that averages similar patches from across the entire image, not just nearby pixels

F.definition: Triangular surfaces in a mesh, each defined by three vertices
The processing history of a file, showing which modules created it and from what source files
Converting a file to another format from the file browser’s Convert to… action (e.g. TIFF↔MRC, OBJ→STL/PLY/glTF).

T.definition: A keyword label attached to a workspace file (raw, annotation, segmentation, and so on) used for filtering and search alongside its category.
A JavaScript 3D graphics library used for rendering and animating 3D content in web browsers
Tagged Image File Format - a flexible image format commonly used in microscopy for storing multi-page image stacks
Three consecutive slices from a stack (z-1, z, z+1) used as input by legacy 2.5D models; current trainings are 2D only

V.definition: Error measured on held-out data not used for training, indicating how well the model generalizes to new images
The corner points of triangles in a mesh, defined by X, Y, Z coordinates
The physical size of one voxel (x, y, z) with a unit; needed to convert voxel counts into physical volumes and surface areas.

O.definition: Wavefront OBJ - a simple text-based 3D geometry format widely supported by 3D software
The degree to which an object blocks light - 100% is fully solid, lower values are more transparent

K.definition: The filter window - a small matrix of weights applied to each pixel and its neighbors

Z.definition: Voxel size along the z (slice) axis relative to the in-plane x/y pixels - set above 1 for anisotropic stacks where slices are spaced farther apart than the in-plane pixel size
Magnification level for viewing images - values above 100% show enlarged detail, below 100% shows a wider view
Joining stacks end to end along the z axis so they continue one another in depth.
